title: Connectors and cohesion
grammar: Linking words (however, although, because, so that, in order to)
function: Link ideas and give coherence to the text

sections.heading: Why connectors matter
sections.body: Connectors (also called linking words or discourse markers) join ideas and make your writing and speaking more coherent. They help the reader or listener follow your argument.

sections.heading: Contrast
table: I was tired, but I finished the work.
It was late. However, we continued working.
Although it was late, we continued.
Despite the rain, we went out.

sections.heading: Cause and reason
table: I stayed home because I was ill.
Since it was raining, we stayed inside.
We stayed inside because of the rain.

sections.heading: Consequence and result
table: I was tired, so I went to bed.
The road was closed; therefore, we took another route.
He studied hard. As a result, he passed.

sections.heading: Purpose
table: I went to the shop to buy bread.
She studies in order to pass the exam.
I left early so that I wouldn't miss the train.

sections.heading: Adding information
list: and: I like tea and coffee.
also: She is a teacher. She is also a writer.
moreover / furthermore (formal): The plan is expensive. Moreover, it is risky.
in addition: In addition, the hotel has a pool.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not confuse 'although' (before a clause) with 'despite' (before a noun).
'Although it was raining' is correct. 'Despite it was raining' is wrong.
'However' is followed by a comma and a new sentence. It does not join two clauses with a comma only.

list.definition: It was expensive. However, I bought it.
Although he was tired, he finished.
Even though it was late, we kept working.
Despite the rain, we went out.
In spite of the noise, I slept well.
On the other hand, it is cheaper.
I stayed home because I was ill.
Since it was raining, we stayed inside.
I was hungry, so I made a sandwich.
He studied hard; therefore, he passed.
As a result, the company grew.
She missed the bus; consequently, she was late.
I came here to help you.
She studies in order to improve.
I left early so that I could rest.
I went to the shop for some bread.
I like tea and coffee.
She speaks English and also French.
The plan is expensive. Moreover, it is risky.
In addition, we offer free delivery.
Furthermore, the results were excellent.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: I stayed home because it was raining.
Although he was tired, he finished the race.
She studied hard, so she passed the exam.
I left early so that I wouldn't miss the train.
It was expensive. However, I bought it.
Despite the rain, we went for a walk.
In order to improve, you should practise every day.
The plan is expensive. Moreover, it is risky.
questions: In sentence 2, what is 'although' used for?
In sentences 3, 4 and 7, what do 'so', 'so that' and 'in order to' introduce?
In sentence 5, why is 'however' followed by a comma?
In sentence 6, what is the difference between 'although' and 'despite'?

questions.prompt: ___ it was late, we decided to keep working.
I studied a lot, ___ I passed the exam.
I stayed home ___ I was ill.
___ the rain, we went to the beach.
I went to the shop ___ buy some bread.
She studies hard ___ pass the exam.
I left early ___ I wouldn't miss the train.
It was raining. ___ , we went out.
questions.explanation: However introduces contrast in a new sentence.

questions.prompt: He worked hard. ___ , he got promoted.
The hotel was expensive. ___ , it was very noisy.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Write a short paragraph (5-6 sentences) about a difficult day using at least 3 different connectors.
Write an opinion paragraph about learning languages using 'because', 'however' and 'so that'.
Rewrite these sentences using different connectors: 'I was tired. I went to bed.' (use: because, so, although).

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Contrast: but, however, although, despite.
Reason: because, since, because of.
Result: so, therefore, as a result.
Purpose: to + verb, in order to, so that.
Adding: and, also, moreover, in addition.
Although + clause. Despite + noun.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not confuse 'although' with 'despite'.
'However' is followed by a comma and a new sentence.
Do not use 'because' with a noun: use 'because of'.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: Although... , ...
Despite + noun, ...
I studied hard, so...
In order to..., I...
Moreover, ...
As a result, ...
